caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
data_source: IMF World Economic Outlook via DataMapper (latest vintage, accessed October 2026)
debt_management: Bulgaria has one of Europe's lowest debt stocks: 22.6% of GDP in 2006, a low of 14.1% in 2010, and only 22.7% in 2020 after the pandemic — remarkably little COVID-era borrowing. It is projected at 27.1% in 2025, the series high, reflecting recent deficits. GDP grew from $34.4bn in 2006 to a projected $131.0bn in 2025. The currency board and conservative fiscal policy are the anchors; debt sustainability is not a question, though the political instability of recent years has complicated budgeting.
inflation_management: Under the currency-board lev peg, Bulgaria imports monetary conditions from abroad. Inflation was 2.5% in 2009, deflationary in 2014 (-1.6%, the series low), then the 2022 shock pushed it to 13%, the series high. Disinflation has been slow: 2.6% in 2024, projected 3.5% for 2025. The delayed convergence toward the Maastricht inflation criterion was a factor in the repeated postponements of euro adoption; persistent services inflation has kept it above the target benchmark.

key_events.event: Global financial crisis ended the pre-crisis boom; the currency board held through a deep correction.
Deflation of -1.6% amid weak demand and low commodity prices.
COVID-19: debt barely moved (22.7% of GDP in 2020), reflecting limited fiscal space used and growth resilience.
Inflation hit 13%; repeated elections produced political instability and delayed euro adoption.
Euro adoption remained on the agenda as inflation converged, with a projected 3.5% in 2025.

outlook_next_decade: Euro adoption is the defining macro event of the next decade if convergence criteria are met; it would cut borrowing costs and remove exchange-rate risk but end the currency board's discipline anchor. Fiscal space is large with debt under 30% of GDP. Risks are political fragmentation stalling reform, and a services-heavy inflation structure that could re-emerge under euro-area conditions. Growth prospects are decent on EU funds and convergence, but demographics weigh.
